# HPagination

> Bounded page navigation with current-page semantics and ellipses for long lists.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.4.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HPagination` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-pagination>`.
- Constructor: `HearthPaginationElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HPagination.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Page numbers are 1-based. total is the item count, not the page count.
- Bounds, previous/next availability, current-page semantics, and ellipses are supplied. Data fetching and URL synchronization belong to the application.

## Public API

modelValue, total, pageSize: number · label: string

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    modelValue?: number;
    total: number;
    pageSize?: number;
    label?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ modelValue: 1, total: 0, pageSize: 20, label: "Pagination" }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(page), change(page)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        page: number
    ];
    change: [
        page: number
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, previous, page, next

Use `hearth-pagination::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HPagination } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const page = ref(1);
function loadPage(page: number) { /* Fetch this page in your application. */ }
</script>

<template>
  <HPagination v-model="page" :total="120" :page-size="20" @change="loadPage" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-pagination');
Object.assign(element, {
  "total": 120,
  "pageSize": 20,
  "modelValue": 1
});

element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [page] = event.detail;
  // Fetch or render the requested page.
});

mount.append(element);
```
